title: HelperPortsSampleResult
description: Result of the helper ports service's sample op: one pass over the host's own tools, and what it found. The four states are answers and not refusals — `unavailable` in particular means this host has no port tool at all, which is the service's answer, so the connection's helper axis stays `serving` and Git and Files keep working on it (design scenario 8). `listeners` and `probesTried` are never null: a reader must not have to tell 'nothing listens' or 'nothing was tried' from 'no answer'.

state.description: The pass's outcome. `available` with an empty listener list means nothing is listening; every other state means the table could not be read.

listeners.description: The listening TCP ports the pass read. Never null: a pass with nothing to report answers [], which is a fact about the host.

probe.description: The rung that produced the sample — ss, netstat, busybox-netstat, lsof or sockstat — and the empty string when no rung produced one. It is what a person is shown as 'which tool answered', so it is reported rather than inferred.

probesTried.description: Every rung this connection has run, in order, each named once. Never null, and deduped because a connection samples for as long as it lives. It is the diagnostics half of `unavailable`: a host with no tools names the four that were looked for.

classification.description: The helper's own sentence about why this is the answer — a timeout, a truncated capture, a tool's refusal, or the ladder having nothing left. Displayed to a person and never matched by a caller: the typed `state` is what a caller switches on.

stderr.description: A bounded excerpt (2 KiB) of the probe's stderr, for a person looking at a host whose tool rejected its flags. Empty when there was nothing to say.

listener.description: One listening TCP port, as the host's own tool reported it.

family.description: The IP family of the bind address.

address.description: The bind address as the probe reported it, which may be a wildcard (0.0.0.0, *, [::]). It is the probe's spelling and not a normalised one: a reader that wants a socket identity derives it.

process.description: The process evidence for one listener. Three-valued and never an empty string: 'nobody owns it' and 'I was not allowed to see' are different facts and are rendered differently.

evidence.description: known — the tool named the owner, so name and pid are valid; permission-denied — the socket is real and its owner was not visible; unsupported — the tool cannot report owners at all (busybox netstat without -p).

name.description: The process name, valid when evidence is `known`.

pid.description: The process id, valid when evidence is `known`.
